**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in CEP290 in individuals with oocyte maturation defect 2, or identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in other genes known to cause Meckel syndrome (e.g., MKS1, TMEM67) in individuals with oocyte maturation defect 2, would falsify this hypothesis of shared mechanism centered on CEP290. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in CEP290 with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01%)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CEP290 in ciliary function and basal body assembly could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common molecular pathways for both developmental disorders.
